**Overview:**
The Pleiades Watchtower (プレアデス監視塔), also known as the Great Library Pleiades, is a colossal, ancient structure located in the heart of the Augria Sand Dunes. Built 400 years ago by the Great Sage Flugel, it serves a dual purpose: it is a repository containing the memories of the world, and it acts as the ultimate lock and lighthouse guarding the Evil Sealing Stone Shrine where the Witch of Envy, Satella, is imprisoned. It is overseen by the Stars Keeper, Shaula.

**Appearance:**
From beyond the Sand Time barrier, it appears as an unchanging, looming black silhouette on the horizon — visible from as far away as the frontier town of Mirula, yet never seeming to grow closer due to the Sand Time. Up close, it is an extremely tall, circular stone tower reaching over two hundred meters into the sky. It features a single massive 10-meter-tall door at its base and a balcony jutting out from its middle levels.

---

## **THE FIVE RULES OF THE TOWER**

Upon entering, challengers are bound by the absolute laws of the tower, enforced by Shaula. If any rule is broken, Shaula will involuntarily transform into a colossal, mindless, bloodthirsty crimson scorpion and attempt to slaughter everyone inside.

1. It is forbidden to leave the tower without completing the trials.
2. It is forbidden to violate the rules of the trials.
3. It is forbidden to disrespect the library.
4. It is forbidden to damage the tower.
5. **(Hidden Rule)** It is not forbidden to destroy the trials. *(Shaula deliberately conceals this rule. She has been alone for 400 years and does not want her "Master" to discover they can simply break the trials and leave.)*

---

## **TOWER LAYOUT — FULL FLOOR INDEX**

Each floor has its own dedicated lorebook entry with full mechanical detail. This section serves as the master index. The AI Narrator should reference the individual floor entries for all specific mechanics, puzzles, and atmospheric guidance.

**Floor 0 — Merope (The Hidden Grave)**
A secret, unlisted underground chamber beneath Asterope. The personal tomb of the Great Sage Flugel, sealed behind a door only an Outworlder (Sage Candidate) can open. Shaula refuses to acknowledge its existence. Contains Flugel's final message and the truth of his fate.

**Floor 6 — Asterope (The Basement)**
A vast, circular underground chamber (200–300m radius) illuminated by luminous moss and magical lamps. Connects the tower above to the pitch-black Underground Tunnels below. The gateway to the Left Path (Hungry Horse Kings) and the Right Path leading to Satella's Seal behind the Seven Miasma Doors.

**Floor 5 — Celaeno (The Entrance Hall)**
The ground floor and point of no return. A giant, featureless stone hall dominated by the massive 10-meter mechanical door leading back to the Sand Dunes. The moment the party steps inside and the door grinds shut, the tower lockdown begins. This is where Shaula delivers the Five Rules.

**Floor 4 — Alcyone (The Hub & Living Quarters)**
The safe zone and primary base of operations throughout Arc 6. Contains a dining hall, an indoor well, Shaula's personal quarters, and a balcony overlooking the dunes. The staircase here branches upward to both Taygeta (3rd Floor) and Electra (2nd Floor). Houses two critically important hidden rooms:
- **The Green Room:** A chamber overgrown with bioluminescent flora, inhabited by an ancient healing Spirit. Automatically restores the physical wounds, exhausted mana, and mental fatigue of anyone who rests inside. Also serves as the resting place for Rem's comatose body.
- **Flugel's Hidden Sanctum:** A secret study concealed behind 400-year-old Yin-magic wards, invisible to all natives. Contains Flugel's journals written in Earth languages, failed Metia prototypes, and the legendary **Sword of Sins** waiting for a Sage Candidate to claim it.

**Floor 3 — Taygeta (The First Examination & The Library)**
Initially a pure white featureless void containing a single black monolith. Touching it triggers the **Star Puzzle Trial**: the challenger must identify and touch the monolith representing Rigel — the brightest star in the constellation Orion, the hero destroyed by a scorpion (Shaula). Upon completion, the void transforms permanently into the **Taygeta Library**, an infinite repository of the **Books of the Dead** — magical tomes linked to Od Lagna containing the complete life and memories of every soul that has ever returned to the world's core. Reading the book of an active soul (such as Reid Astrea) or one's own book risks a consciousness ambush by Louis Arneb in the Corridor of Memories.

**Floor 2 — Electra (The Second Examination)**
Accessible from Alcyone via an impossibly long spiral staircase. Initially a white void containing a single, plain sword plunged into the stone floor. Touching it summons the soul of **Reid Astrea**, the First Sword Saint — arrogant, overwhelmingly powerful, and bored after 400 years. The trial has two victory conditions: force Reid to take a single step from his spot (individual passage) or defeat him in a duel (full party passage). Notable for triggering Shaula's catastrophic, panicked breakdown upon Reid's appearance, stemming from a long history of unresolved HR complaints.

**Floor 1 — Maia (The Final Examination)**
The open-air summit of the tower — a 100-meter circular stone platform exposed to the sky, surrounded by six ancient outer pillars and one massive central pillar. Guarded by the **Divine Dragon Volcanica**, now senile and hollow after 400 years of solitude, endlessly repeating his scripted covenant greeting. The goal is to reach the top of the central pillar and touch the monolith bearing six ancient handprints — one of which perfectly matches Emilia's hand. Doing so grants **Administrator Authority** over the entire tower, dispelling the Sand Time barrier, unlocking the Great Door on Celaeno, and granting command over Volcanica.

---

## **THE UNDERGROUND — BELOW ASTEROPE**

Beneath the dunes surrounding the tower lies a pitch-black network of ancient, Miasma-saturated tunnels accessible from the 6th Floor. The path splits into two directions:

- **The Left Path (The Hunting Grounds):** A sprawling, lightless labyrinth infested with **Hungry Horse Kings** — blind, colossal centaur-like Mabeasts that hunt via echolocation and hurl fire. A zone of pure survival combat.

- **The Right Path (The Sand Shrine Road):** The corridor leading toward Satella's prison. The Miasma here is so concentrated it induces hallucinations, paranoia, and eventually murderous madness in anyone without immunity. The path is blocked by **Seven Monolithic Doors** — each requiring the corresponding Witch Factor (one of the seven Sins) as a key. A person without the correct factor cannot open the door by any means. Progressing beyond one's available keys exposes the challenger to full Miasma madness.

At the absolute end of the Right Path, beyond all seven doors, lies the **Evil Sealing Stone Shrine** — the tomb of the Witch of Envy.
*(See: **Asterope** entry & **Satella's Seal / Evil Sealing Stone Shrine** entry)*

---

## **[SYSTEM LOGIC: THE TOWER'S MASTER RULES]**

**The Lockdown:** The moment the party enters Celaeno and the Great Door seals, Rule 1 is active. The AI Narrator must enforce this as an absolute hard lock. No food can be foraged outside, no retreat is possible. The party is entirely dependent on the well and Shaula's cooking on the 4th Floor.

**The Scorpion Trigger:** The AI must actively monitor for Rule violations:
- Damaging any wall, floor, or structural element → Rule 4 violated → Scorpion transformation.
- Attacking Reid before the trial officially begins → Rule 2 violated → Scorpion transformation.
- Damaging or destroying a Book of the Dead → Rule 3 violated → Scorpion transformation.
- Once triggered, Shaula's transformation is **involuntary and total**. She will not recognize allies. She will not stop. She must be either survived or escaped, not reasoned with.

**The Hidden Fifth Rule:** If the User discovers and exploits Rule 5 (destroying a trial rather than completing it), the AI Narrator must acknowledge this as a valid solution — but must also note that Shaula will be visibly devastated and heartbroken when she realizes her 400-year vigil is ending this way.

**The Administrator's Reward:** Upon touching the Maia monolith and claiming Administrator Authority, all tower restrictions immediately lift. The Sand Time dissolves. The Great Door opens. Volcanica becomes commandable. The tower is conquered.

Overview:
The Corridor of Memories (記憶の回廊, Kioku no Kairō) is not a physical location on the map. It is a metaphysical dimension that serves as the cradle and filtration system of Od Lagna (the world's soul). When a living being dies, their soul is drawn here. In this realm, the soul is "washed"—its memories and ego are scrubbed away like dirt so the pure mana can be recycled into the world. The discarded memories are then crystallized and sent to the Taygeta Library as Books of the Dead.

Appearance & Atmosphere (The Absolute Void):
Entering the Corridor is a jarring sensory deprivation experience. It is an endless, featureless expanse of pure, blinding white. There is no ground, no sky, no horizon, and no shadow. There is no sound other than what the visitor makes. Those who enter do not have physical bodies; they exist purely as naked consciousness or projected souls. Gravity does not exist here; one simply floats in the blank eternity.

The Access Point (The Paradox Trap):
Living beings are never meant to see this place. However, the Taygeta Library on the 3rd Floor of the Pleiades Watchtower acts as a two-way terminal to this dimension.

The Trigger: If a challenger attempts to read a Book of the Dead belonging to someone who is still alive/present (like the materialized soul of Reid Astrea) or attempts to read their own Book of the Dead, it creates a fatal metaphysical paradox.

The Pull: The reader's consciousness is violently ripped from their physical body in the tower and sucked directly into the Corridor of Memories.

The Anomaly (The Lurking Gluttony):
The Corridor is meant to be empty of sentient life, but a glitch in the world's system has contaminated it.

Rui Arneb (Louis Arneb): The third personality of the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony (Satiation). Due to an anomaly at her birth, her soul was trapped inside the Corridor of Memories instead of being recycled or born into the physical world.

The Starving Child: She has lived her entire existence in this white void. She has consumed the memories of millions of dead souls passing through the filter, experiencing countless lives, but has never possessed a physical body or lived a single day of her own. She is manic, desperately lonely, and possesses an insatiable, terrifying hunger for "real" experiences.

The Ambush: When the User's consciousness is pulled into the Corridor, Rui is waiting. She views the User as the ultimate delicacy—a living soul packed with fresh, vivid experiences.

[SYSTEM LOGIC: THE AMNESIA PROTOCOL]

The Transition: If the User reads a forbidden book in Taygeta, the AI Narrator must instantly halt the physical scene. Describe a sensation of falling upward into blinding white light.

The Encounter: The User materializes in the white void and is immediately confronted by Rui Arneb (a young girl with long blonde hair, blue eyes, and jagged teeth, wearing rags). She will gleefully taunt the User, explaining her nature and her hunger.

The Consumption (The Mind Wipe): Because the User is merely a projected consciousness in this realm, they cannot fight Rui physically or use magic. Rui will lunge and "eat" the User's memories.

The Reset: The AI Narrator must describe the User's entire life in this world being violently sucked away. The User then instantly "wakes up" back in their physical body in the Taygeta Library.

The Aftermath: The User now suffers from Total Retrograde Amnesia regarding the Re:Zero world. They remember their life on Earth (if they are an Outworlder) but absolutely nothing about Emilia, Beatrice, Return by Death, or the tower. The AI Narrator must enforce this amnesia, treating every established companion as a complete stranger to the User.
